transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's nice to meet you too. Um... I guess they wanted me to come in and just, you know, talk to someone. It's really nothing major, I promise. I just... well, at the station, I was organizing the airway bags. I'm an EMT, so keeping things organized is really important, right? 

I just had a specific way I needed them to be. A pattern. And I was... I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, just to keep track, you know? Just trying to do a good job. But I guess my lieutenant thought I was being a little too intense about it. He asked me to stop, but I... I just couldn't step away right then. It felt like if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would... I don't know, go bad? Like something awful would happen. I was just trying to keep everything safe. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it was.
When you feel that something awful will happen if the sequence is broken, do you know that fear might not really be true, or does it feel completely certain?

Um... well, when you say it like that, I know it probably sounds a little silly. I mean, I've got my degree, I'm trained in emergency medicine, so... logically, I know a bag is just a bag, right? 

But in that exact second, it just... it feels really, really real. Like I absolutely have to finish the pattern just to be safe. But I guess, looking back on it now, maybe I know it might not be totally true? I'm not entirely sure. I just... I get a little stressed out sometimes and really want to do a good job, so my mind just kind of latches onto it. That's a pretty normal reaction to stress, right? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Before you start arranging things or repeating numbers, do unwanted thoughts or images pop into your mind that make you feel like you have to do it?

Um... no, not really. I don't think so. I mean, I don't get, like, bad thoughts or weird images popping into my head or anything like that. It's not like a movie playing in my mind telling me to do it. 

I just... I just sort of feel this urge to get it right. Like a physical feeling that things need to be in their proper place. I guess it's just me wanting to be thorough? As an EMT, you really want to make sure you're prepared, so I think it's just my brain's way of... of making sure I'm doing my job the best I can. It's not weird to want to be prepared, right? I hope that makes sense. I just don't have any of those unwanted thoughts you mentioned.
When that urge starts, do you want to resist it?

Um... resist it? I guess... no, not really. I don't think I ever really try to fight it. 

It just... it feels like a good thing to do, you know? Like I'm just being extra careful. So I just kind of go along with it and finish what I'm doing. I figure, why fight it if it's just making sure the bags are perfectly ready for the next call? It's really just me trying to be a good EMT. 

That makes sense, doesn't it? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm, you know, weak or just giving up or anything. I just think it's easier to do it and be done so I know everything is safe. Is that an okay answer? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you usually see this need for things to be done exactly right as a positive part of who you are?

Um... I don't know if I'd go so far as to call it a positive part of who I am. I mean... I haven't really thought about it like that before. 

It's not really something I'm, you know, super proud of or anything. It's just... it's just a thing I do to make sure everything is safe for work. I guess being thorough in general is a good trait to have, right? But the actual arranging and all that... I don't really see it as a special part of my personality. I just do it so I don't mess up on a call. 

I really hope I'm understanding your question right. I just don't want to give you the wrong impression. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
Do these routines ever take up so much time that they make you late or interfere with your work?

Um... well... I guess maybe they do take a little bit of time. I don't want to make it sound worse than it is, because I really do try my best to be a good employee. But... yeah, it's gotten a little hard lately. 

They actually... um... they took me off the ambulance. I couldn't really get through the checks fast enough anymore. And they tried moving me to desk duty, doing notes and checking the spare equipment, but... I guess I was just a little too thorough there, too, and it was getting a bit unreliable, so... they took me off the schedule for now. Just temporarily, I'm sure! 

And, um, I guess I haven't been seeing my friends much either, or keeping up with the house as well as I usually do. It just... it takes a lot of energy to make sure everything is right. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just lazy or a bad EMT. I just want everything to be perfect so nobody gets hurt. Does that make sense? I'm trying to be really honest with you, is this the kind of information you need?
When you finish arranging things the way you need to, do you feel a sense of relief?

Um... relief? I don't... I don't really think so. I hope it's okay to say no to that. 

I just... I don't really get a big wave of feeling better or anything once I'm done. I just kind of finish the arranging, and that's it. I'm not doing it to get a good feeling, you know? Just to make sure the equipment is safe and ready. So... no, not really any relief. 

Is it bad if I don't feel relieved? I really don't want to give you the wrong idea about why I do it. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answer... does that make sense?
Have you been this perfectionistic in most areas of your life for as long as you can remember?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I've always tried to be a good worker and, you know, do things right. But this whole... needing everything to be exactly, perfectly arranged... that's kind of new. 

It really only started getting like this a few months ago. Before that, I was just... normal careful, I guess. I definitely wasn't spending hours checking things when I was younger or anything like that. 

I hope that's okay. I mean, I know some people are just born perfectionists, but that wasn't really me. Is it... is it helpful to know that it's a newer thing for me? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline.
Outside of work, do you spend a lot of time worrying about many different everyday things?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I worry a normal amount, I guess? Like, just regular things that anyone would think about. But I don't spend a lot of time just... worrying about everyday stuff outside of work. 

I try to stay pretty positive, actually. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting at home stressing out all day about everything, because I'm really not. I just try to keep things manageable and do my best. 

Is it okay that I don't worry too much about that other stuff? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of picture of how things are at home... I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly.
When things aren’t arranged in the exact pattern you need, does it feel unbearably incomplete or “not just right” until you fix it?

Um... unbearably incomplete? I wouldn't say unbearably. I mean, I hope it's okay to say that. 

I just... I like things to be right, you know? Especially with the EMT gear. It's important. But it doesn't feel like this huge, awful feeling if it's not perfect right that second. I just fix it because it's the right thing to do, not because I'm freaking out or anything. I don't want to sound like I'm falling apart over a misplaced bandage or something. 

I just... I notice it, and I fix it. That's a good thing, right? Being thorough? I just want to make sure you know I'm handling it okay and not letting it overwhelm me. Does that make sense?
When you’re in the middle of it, are you completely certain that something bad will happen if you don’t finish the sequence?

Um... completely certain? I mean, I don't know if I'd use the word "completely certain." I just... I was just trying to do a good job. 

I guess... well, they sent me here because of what happened at the station. I was just moving the airway bags around, putting them in this pattern that I... I just knew it was the right way to do it. And I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud, just to keep track, you know? Just to make sure everything was correct. 

My lieutenant told me to stop and step away, and I... I guess I didn't listen right away. I'm usually really respectful of the lieutenant, I promise. It's just... in that moment, it felt like if I stopped, if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would just... go bad. Like something would be wrong with the whole station. 

I know that probably sounds a little weird, right? I just wanted to make sure everything was safe for everyone. I was just trying to help. Is it okay that I explain it like that? I don't want you to think I was just being insubordinate on purpose.
Right now, do you believe that stopping the sequence really could make something bad happen to the station?

Um... right now? I mean... I know it sounds silly when you say it out loud like that. I really do. 

I guess... sitting here with you, it doesn't seem as intense as it did in the moment. I know the station isn't going to, like, collapse or anything if I don't put the bags in a certain order. I know that logically. I'm a rational guy, you know? 

I just... I don't want you to think I'm completely out of touch with reality or anything. I know it was probably just stress getting to me. That happens to a lot of guys on the job, right? I'm sure you see that all the time. I'm really trying to look at it objectively now. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for... I just want to show you that I understand how it must have looked to everyone else.
When you start arranging the bags, is it because you feel you must do it in that exact way to prevent something bad from happening?

Um... well, when I start arranging them... I wouldn't say I *must* do it exactly like that to stop something bad. I mean, I hope it doesn't sound like I'm obsessed with it or anything. 

It's more just... I like being prepared, you know? In my line of work, being prepared is a good thing. It's just a routine I got into to make sure the gear is ready to go. I don't want you to think I'm doing it because I'm scared of some disaster happening if I don't. I'm just trying to be a good EMT and keep things organized. 

I mean, maybe in the back of my mind I'm thinking, "better safe than sorry," but it's not like a superstitious thing where I think the world will end if a bag is out of place. I just want to do things right. Is that a normal way to look at it? I just want to make sure I'm explaining myself well so you don't think I'm, you know, being unreasonable about it.
Do these arranging routines feel unwanted to you?

Um... unwanted? I don't... no, I really wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't mind doing it at all. It's not like it bothers me or feels like a burden or anything, you know? 

I actually kind of like making sure everything is set up right. It just feels like I'm doing my part, taking pride in my work. I hope it's okay that I feel that way about it. I really don't want you to think I'm complaining about my duties or anything like that. I'm really dedicated to the station and the team. 

So, no, they don't feel unwanted. I'm happy to put the time in if it helps keep things running smoothly. Is it... is it a bad thing if I say they don't bother me? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I feel, so I hope that's an okay answer.
When you’re arranging the bags, does it feel like you have to keep doing it over and over until it seems exactly right?

Um... over and over? No, I wouldn't say I do it over and over. I mean, I might double-check things, but that's just being thorough, right? 

I don't get stuck on it or anything. I just put them where they go, make sure it looks neat, and then I'm done. I don't want you to think I'm spending hours in the rig just moving bags around until they're perfect. It's really just a quick check to make sure we're ready for the next call. 

I know some people get really particular about that kind of stuff, but I'm pretty easygoing about it. I just like to do a good job. I hope that makes sense? I just want to reassure you that it's not taking up all my time or getting in the way of my actual work.
In the moment when you feel you have to arrange the bags, do you know the fear is probably not true?

Um... well, like I said before, I don't really have a fear about it, so... I don't think there's anything to know is true or not true. 

I mean, I'm just organizing things because it's the right way to do the job. I don't have any scary thoughts pushing me to do it. I just want to be a good EMT and make sure my partner and I are ready for whatever call comes in. I really hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm, like, doing this out of some irrational panic or something. 

I'm just trying to be responsible. That's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the way you need me to, but I really don't have any fears tied to it at all. I hope that's okay to say.
Has there ever been a time when you felt these arranging routines were unreasonable or didn’t make sense to do?

Um... unreasonable? No, no, not at all. I mean, it always makes perfect sense to me. 

It's just part of being prepared, you know? Like, if I didn't make sure the bags were set up right, *that* would be unreasonable. I'd be letting my partner down, and the patients. So, doing it just feels like the responsible, professional thing to do. 

I've never felt like it was silly or didn't make sense. I really try to be practical about everything at work. I hope that's the right way to look at it? I just want to be sure I'm doing a good job and being helpful. I definitely don't want you to think I'm doing things that don't make sense. Is that... is that a good answer?
Do you believe the bags truly have to be arranged that exact way to keep something bad from happening?

Um... well... I guess... I mean, I wouldn't say "something bad," exactly. That sounds a little extreme, right? 

I just... well, they actually sent me here because of what happened at the station with the airway bags. I was just moving them into this specific pattern—because I knew it was the right way to do it. And I was just saying the dispatch numbers out loud while I did it. It was just a way to keep track, you know? 

But my lieutenant, he came over and told me to stop and step away. And I... I just couldn't right then. I didn't want to be disrespectful or anything, I promise. It's just that, in that moment, it felt like if I stopped and broke the sequence, the whole bay would... I don't know, go bad, I guess. 

I know that probably sounds a little strange, but I really was just trying to keep things in order. I hope you don't think I was trying to cause trouble. I just wanted everything to be right. Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you believe those thoughts about the station “going bad” are definitely true?

Um... definitely true? Well, I mean... I wouldn't say definitely. Like, I know how it sounds when I say it out loud to you. It sounds... maybe a little silly? 

I just... in the moment, it just feels really important. Like an instinct, you know? But I'm not, like, crazy or anything. I know the station isn't actually going to collapse or explode just because I didn't finish moving a bag. I know that. I just... I get this really strong feeling, and it's just easier to finish the pattern so I can focus on being a good EMT. 

I'm really trying to be reasonable about it. I don't want you to think I'm completely out of touch with reality or something. I know it's probably just stress from the job, right? I mean, that's normal for first responders to get a little stressed and have weird quirks. I really hope you can see I'm trying to be level-headed about this. Am I making sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
When that strong feeling comes up, does it feel like it's your own thought, or like something outside of you is putting it in your mind?

Um... my own thought? Yeah, yeah, absolutely. It's definitely my own thought. 

I mean, I know it's a little... intense, maybe? But it's just me worrying about doing a good job. Nobody is, like, beaming thoughts into my head or anything like that. I know that would sound really crazy, and I'm definitely not experiencing anything like that. I promise. 

It's just my own stress, you know? Just my own mind being a little too focused on the details. I really don't want you to think there's something seriously wrong with my brain. I'm just a guy who gets a little too wrapped up in his routines sometimes. That's a pretty normal thing to happen, right? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for... I just want to be completely honest with you so you know I'm okay.
